pages.text: A sample of n measurements has a mean that wanders by σ/√n, its standard error. To be sure at confidence z (2 for about 95%, 2.58 for 99%), the margin z·σ/√n must be small. Four times the sample halves the margin.
$(thing)Set$(): Sample size, Confidence.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): A jarred board: the spread varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none beyond the recipe windows.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Smaller samples are faster.
